name: Greener by Default
beneficiaries_note: The countries the model's summary names, sharing equally: United States, United Kingdom.

missing_data.note: Thin: ACE's estimate of a campaign or outreach programme: the animals or people its work reached and the welfare change per animal are ACE's judgments (pledges won, meals swapped, welfare footprints), with no controlled evaluation of the charity.

summary: Helps hospitals, universities, stadiums and corporate cafeterias in the United States and United Kingdom serve plant-based meals by default. A re-implementation of Animal Charity Evaluators' 2026 cost-effectiveness sheet: its Healthcare, Business & Industry and College & University programmes against all of Greener by Default's 2025 to mid-2026 spending, research included. One hospital engagement carries about 90% of the modelled impact. ACE's own estimate is 2.1 SADs per dollar, and about 44% of it falls on shrimp, which count at a tenth of a chicken.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model, not ACE's. The meals replaced spare shrimp, chickens, fish and mammals; each species' share of the SADs is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain with Rethink Priorities' welfare ranges. How a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the one animal slider, under Your values.

rows.label: Fall in production per meal not eaten
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: when fewer meals with animal products are eaten, prices fall and others eat a little more, so production falls by less (facts: sad_factors.production_response). Every diet-change model multiplies the suffering of meals replaced by it. ACE counts one meal less served as one meal less produced (1), kept in the evaluator view.

rows.label: ACE's result without shrimp (SADs per dollar)

source.title: ACE, CEA Context tab (robustness): 'Excluding shrimps from the estimate results in 1.19 SADs/$'

rows.explainer: ACE notes that shrimp is about 53% of its standard US meal replacement estimate, though not plausibly half the animal impact of a hospital entrée.

rows.label: Share of the SADs that falls on shrimp
rows.explainer: One minus ACE's result without shrimp over its result with it (both on the same years): 44%. ACE puts shrimp at about 53% of its standard meal estimate, which carries about 90% of the result.

rows.label: Share of the non-shrimp SADs that falls on chickens
rows.explainer: Ours. ACE doesn't publish the species split of its 2026 US meal estimate. From ACE's 2026 SADs per animal (a fast-growing broiler 5.2, a battery-caged hen 29.5 a year, a farmed salmon 44.3 a year, a sow 104 a year, a dairy cow 853 a year) and US consumption per person (about 25 broilers and 1 hen's eggs a year, a few farmed fish, a small share of a pig and a cow), chickens carry about two thirds of the rest. Range is ours.

rows.label: Share of the non-shrimp, non-chicken SADs that falls on fish
rows.explainer: Ours, from the same rough reckoning: farmed fish about a fifth of the non-shrimp SADs, mammals (pigs and cattle, counted as pigs, as the shared meal shares do) about a sixth. Range is ours.

rows.label: Pain days averted per dollar you give: shrimp
rows.explainer: ACE's 2026 SADs are days of pain weighted by intensity only, with no species weight: every species' SADs in ACE's 2026 SADs summary add up its pain-scaled days alone (a battery-caged hen: 131.28 × 0.057 + 62.75 × 0.245 + 6.69 = 29.55), and Ambitious Impact made the unscaled figure its main output in April 2026. So they enter as days of this species' disabling pain.
